verses.1:1: The words of Nehemiah the son of Hacaliah. Now it came to pass in the month of Chislev, in the twentieth year, that I was in Shushan the citadel.
verses.1:2: And Hanani, one of my brethren, came, he and men from Judah; and I asked them concerning the Jews who had escaped, who remained from the captivity, and concerning Jerusalem.
verses.1:3: And they said to me, "Those who remain, who are left from the captivity there in the province, are in great affliction and reproach; the wall of Jerusalem is also breached, and its gates have been burned with fire."
verses.1:4: Now it came to pass, upon hearing these words, that I sat down and wept, and I mourned for days; and I continued fasting and praying before the God of heaven.
verses.1:5: And I said, "I pray, O LORD, God of heaven, the great and awesome God, who keeps the covenant and lovingkindness with those who love Him and with those who keep His commandments:
verses.1:6: Let Your ear now be attentive, and Your eyes be open, that You may hear the prayer of Your servant which I am praying before You this day, day and night, for the children of Israel Your servants, and confessing the sins of the children of Israel which we have sinned against You; both I and my father's house have sinned.
verses.1:7: We have acted very corruptly against You, and have not kept the commandments, nor the statutes, nor the ordinances that You commanded Your servant Moses.
verses.1:8: Remember, I pray, the word that You commanded Your servant Moses, saying, 'If you act unfaithfully, I will scatter you among the peoples;
verses.1:9: but if you return to Me, and keep My commandments and do them, though your outcasts be at the farthest reaches of the heavens, yet from there I will gather them and bring them to the place that I have chosen to cause My name to dwell there.'
verses.1:10: Now these are Your servants and Your people, whom You have redeemed by Your great power and by Your mighty hand.
verses.1:11: O Lord, I pray, let Your ear now be attentive to the prayer of Your servant, and to the prayer of Your servants who delight to fear Your name; and grant success, I pray, to Your servant this day, and grant him mercy in the sight of this man." Now I was cupbearer to the king.
verses.2:1: And it came to pass in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, when wine was before him, that I took up the wine and gave it to the king. Now I had not previously been sad in his presence.
verses.2:2: Therefore the king said to me, "Why is your countenance sad, since you are not sick? This is nothing other than sorrow of heart." Then I became exceedingly afraid,
verses.2:3: and I said to the king, "May the king live forever! Why should my countenance not be sad, when the city, the place of the tombs of my fathers, lies waste, and its gates have been consumed by fire?"
verses.2:4: Then the king said to me, "For what do you make request?" So I prayed to the God of heaven.
verses.2:5: And I said to the king, "If it seems good to the king, and if your servant has found favor in your sight, I ask that you send me to Judah, to the city of the tombs of my fathers, that I may rebuild it."
verses.2:6: Then the king said to me—the queen also sitting beside him—"How long shall your journey be, and when will you return?" So it pleased the king to send me, and I set him a time.
verses.2:7: Moreover I said to the king, "If it seems good to the king, let letters be given to me for the governors beyond the River, that they may allow me to pass through until I come to Judah;
verses.2:8: and a letter to Asaph, the keeper of the king's forest, that he may give me timber to make beams for the gates of the citadel belonging to the temple, and for the wall of the city, and for the house that I shall occupy." And the king granted them to me, according to the good hand of my God upon me.
verses.2:9: Then I came to the governors beyond the River and delivered to them the letters of the king. Now the king had sent captains of the army and horsemen with me.
verses.2:10: When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard of it, it greatly displeased them that a man had come to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.
verses.2:11: So I came to Jerusalem and was there three days.
verses.2:12: Then I arose in the night, I and a few men with me; and I told no one what my God had put in my heart to do for Jerusalem; nor was there any beast with me, except the beast on which I rode.
verses.2:13: And I went out by night through the Valley Gate, toward the Dragon Well and to the Dung Gate, and I inspected the walls of Jerusalem which were broken down, and its gates which had been consumed by fire.
verses.2:14: Then I passed on to the Fountain Gate and to the King's Pool, but there was no room for the beast under me to pass.
verses.2:15: So I went up in the night by the valley and inspected the wall; then I turned back and entered by the Valley Gate, and so returned.
verses.2:16: And the officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing; nor had I as yet told the Jews, or the priests, or the nobles, or the officials, or the rest who did the work.
verses.2:17: Then I said to them, "You see the distress that we are in, how Jerusalem lies waste and its gates are burned with fire. Come, and let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, that we may no longer be a reproach."
verses.2:18: And I told them of the hand of my God that had been good upon me, and also of the words of the king that he had spoken to me. And they said, "Let us arise and build." So they strengthened their hands for the good work.
verses.2:19: But when Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite official, and Geshem the Arab heard of it, they mocked us and despised us, and said, "What is this thing that you are doing? Will you rebel against the king?"
verses.2:20: So I answered them and said to them, "The God of heaven Himself will prosper us; therefore we, His servants, will arise and build, but you have no portion, nor right, nor memorial in Jerusalem."
verses.3:1: Then Eliashib the high priest arose with his brethren the priests and built the Sheep Gate; they consecrated it and set up its doors; they consecrated it as far as the Tower of the Hundred, and as far as the Tower of Hananel.
verses.3:2: And next to him the men of Jericho built. And next to him Zaccur the son of Imri built.
verses.3:3: Also the sons of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate; they laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars.
verses.3:4: And next to them Meremoth the son of Uriah, the son of Hakkoz, made repairs. And next to them Meshullam the son of Berechiah, the son of Meshezabel, made repairs. And next to them Zadok the son of Baana made repairs.
verses.3:5: And next to them the Tekoites made repairs; but their nobles did not put their necks to the work of their lords.
verses.3:6: Moreover Joiada the son of Paseah and Meshullam the son of Besodeiah repaired the Old Gate; they laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars.
verses.3:8: Next to him Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs. And next to him Hananiah, one of the perfumers, made repairs; and they restored Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.
verses.3:9: And next to them Rephaiah the son of Hur, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, made repairs.
verses.3:10: And next to them Jedaiah the son of Harumaph made repairs opposite his house. And next to him Hattush the son of Hashabneiah made repairs.
verses.3:11: Malchijah the son of Harim and Hashub the son of Pahath-Moab repaired another section, as well as the Tower of the Ovens.
verses.3:12: And next to him Shallum the son of Hallohesh, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, made repairs, he and his daughters.
verses.3:13: Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate; they built it and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars, and repaired a thousand cubits of the wall as far as the Dung Gate.
verses.3:14: And Malchijah the son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth-Haccerem, repaired the Dung Gate; he built it and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars.
verses.3:15: And Shallun the son of Col-Hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate; he built it, roofed it, and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars, and he also repaired the wall of the Pool of Shelah by the King's Garden, as far as the stairs that descend from the City of David.
verses.3:16: After him Nehemiah the son of Azbuk, ruler of half the district of Beth-Zur, made repairs as far as a point opposite the tombs of David, and as far as the artificial pool, and as far as the House of the Mighty Men.
verses.3:17: After him the Levites made repairs: Rehum the son of Bani. Next to him Hashabiah, ruler of half the district of Keilah, made repairs for his district.
verses.3:18: After him their brethren made repairs: Bavvai the son of Henadad, ruler of half the district of Keilah.
verses.3:19: And next to him Ezer the son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired another section opposite the ascent to the armory at the angle.
verses.3:20: After him Baruch the son of Zaccai zealously repaired another section, from the angle to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
verses.3:21: After him Meremoth the son of Uriah, the son of Hakkoz, repaired another section, from the door of the house of Eliashib even to the end of the house of Eliashib.
verses.3:22: And after him the priests, the men of the plain, made repairs.
verses.3:23: After him Benjamin and Hashub made repairs opposite their house. After him Azariah the son of Maaseiah, the son of Ananiah, made repairs beside his house.
verses.3:24: After him Binnui the son of Henadad repaired another section, from the house of Azariah to the angle, and even to the corner.
verses.3:25: Palal the son of Uzai made repairs opposite the angle, and the tower projecting from the upper house of the king that is by the court of the guard. After him Pedaiah the son of Parosh made repairs.
verses.3:26: Moreover the temple servants dwelling on Ophel made repairs as far as a point opposite the Water Gate toward the east, and the projecting tower.
verses.3:27: After him the Tekoites repaired another section, from opposite the great projecting tower even to the wall of Ophel.
verses.3:28: Above the Horse Gate the priests made repairs, each one opposite his own house.
verses.3:29: After him Zadok the son of Immer made repairs opposite his own house. And after him Shemaiah the son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the East Gate, made repairs.
verses.3:30: After him Hananiah the son of Shelemiah, and Hanun the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another section. After him Meshullam the son of Berechiah made repairs opposite his chamber.
verses.3:31: After him Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs as far as the house of the temple servants and of the merchants, opposite the Inspection Gate, and as far as the upper chamber of the corner.
verses.3:32: And between the upper chamber of the corner and the Sheep Gate, the goldsmiths and the merchants made repairs.
verses.3:33: Now it came to pass, when Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, that he was furious and greatly indignant, and mocked the Jews.
verses.3:34: And he spoke before his brethren and the army of Samaria, and said, "What are these feeble Jews doing? Will they restore it for themselves? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they finish it in a day? Will they revive the stones out of the heaps of dust, burned as they are?"
verses.3:35: Now Tobiah the Ammonite was beside him, and he said, "Even what they are building—if a fox should go up on it, he would break down their stone wall!"
verses.3:36: Hear, O our God, for we are despised; turn their reproach back upon their own head, and give them over as plunder in a land of captivity.
verses.3:37: Do not cover their iniquity, and do not let their sin be blotted out from before You; for they have provoked You to anger in the sight of the builders.
verses.4:1: Now it came to pass, when Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites heard that the restoration of the walls of Jerusalem was advancing and that the breaches had begun to be closed, that they became exceedingly angry.
verses.4:2: And all of them conspired together to come and fight against Jerusalem and to cause confusion in it.
verses.4:3: But we prayed to our God, and we stationed a watch against them day and night on account of them.
verses.4:4: Then Judah said, "The strength of the burden bearers is failing, and the rubble is abundant, so we are not able to build on the wall."
verses.4:5: And our adversaries said, "They will neither know nor see until we come into their midst and slay them, and cause the work to cease."
verses.4:6: And it came to pass, when the Jews who dwelt near them came, that they said to us ten times, "From every place to which you turn, they will come upon us."
verses.4:7: Therefore I positioned them in the lowest parts of the space behind the wall, in the exposed places; indeed, I stationed the people according to their families, with their swords, their spears, and their bows.
verses.4:8: And I looked, and I arose and said to the nobles, to the officials, and to the rest of the people, "Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome, and fight for your brethren, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your houses."
verses.4:9: And it came to pass, when our enemies heard that it had become known to us, and that God had brought their counsel to nothing, that all of us returned to the wall, each man to his work.
verses.4:10: And it came to pass from that day onward that half of my servants labored at the work, while the other half held the spears, the shields, the bows, and the coats of mail; and the leaders stood behind the whole house of Judah.
verses.4:11: Those who built on the wall and those who carried burdens, loading them—each with one of his hands performed the work, and with the other held a weapon.
verses.4:12: And the builders each had his sword bound at his side as they built; and the one who sounded the trumpet was beside me.
verses.4:13: Then I said to the nobles, to the officials, and to the rest of the people, "The work is great and extensive, and we are separated upon the wall, each man far from his brother.
verses.4:14: In whatever place you hear the sound of the trumpet, gather to us there. Our God will fight for us."
verses.4:15: So we labored at the work, while half of them held the spears from the rising of the dawn until the stars appeared.
verses.4:16: At that same time I also said to the people, "Let each man and his servant lodge within Jerusalem, that they may be a watch for us by night, and labor by day."
verses.4:17: So neither I, nor my brethren, nor my servants, nor the men of the watch who followed me—none of us took off our garments; each man kept his weapon even at the water.
verses.5:1: Now there arose a great outcry of the people and of their wives against their brethren the Jews.
verses.5:2: For there were those who said, "With our sons and our daughters, we are many; let us obtain grain, that we may eat and live."
verses.5:3: There were also those who said, "We are pledging our fields, our vineyards, and our houses, that we may obtain grain in the famine."
verses.5:4: And there were those who said, "We have borrowed silver for the king's tribute upon our fields and our vineyards.
verses.5:5: Yet now our flesh is as the flesh of our brethren, and our children are as their children; and behold, we are forcing our sons and our daughters to be slaves, and some of our daughters are already brought into bondage. It is not in the power of our hand to help it, for our fields and our vineyards belong to others."
verses.5:6: And I became exceedingly angry when I heard their outcry and these words.
verses.5:7: Then I took counsel with myself, and I contended with the nobles and with the officials, and said to them, "You are exacting interest, each man from his brother." And I called a great assembly against them.
verses.5:8: And I said to them, "According to our ability we have bought back our brethren the Jews who were sold to the nations; and will you now even sell your brethren, that they should be sold to us?" Then they kept silent and could not find a word to say.
verses.5:9: And I said, "The thing that you are doing is not good. Should you not walk in the fear of our God because of the reproach of the nations, our enemies?
verses.5:10: I also, with my brethren and my servants, am lending them silver and grain. Please, let us leave off this exacting of interest.
verses.5:11: Restore to them this very day their fields, their vineyards, their olive groves, and their houses, as well as the hundredth part of the silver, the grain, the new wine, and the oil that you are exacting from them."
verses.5:12: Then they said, "We will restore it and will require nothing from them; we will do just as you say." So I summoned the priests and put them under oath to do according to this word.
verses.5:13: I also shook out the fold of my garment and said, "Thus may God shake out from his house and from his labor every man who does not keep this promise; thus may he be shaken out and emptied." And all the assembly said, "Amen," and praised the LORD. And the people did according to this promise.
verses.5:14: Moreover, from the day that I was appointed to be their governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year even to the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes—twelve years—neither I nor my brethren ate the bread of the governor.
verses.5:15: But the former governors who were before me laid heavy burdens upon the people, and took from them bread and wine, besides forty shekels of silver; indeed, even their servants exercised dominion over the people. But I did not do so, because of the fear of God.
verses.5:16: Moreover, I also persevered in the work of this wall, and we acquired no land; and all my servants were gathered there for the work.
verses.5:17: Furthermore, one hundred and fifty men, Jews and officials, were at my table, besides those who came to us from the nations that were around us.
verses.5:18: Now what was prepared for each day was one ox and six choice sheep; also fowl were prepared for me, and once every ten days an abundance of all kinds of wine. Yet for all this, I did not demand the bread of the governor, because the service lay heavy upon this people.
verses.5:19: Remember me, O my God, for good, for all that I have done for this people.
verses.6:1: Now it came to pass, when it was heard by Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies that I had built the wall and that no breach remained in it, though up to that time I had not set up the doors in the gates,
verses.6:2: that Sanballat and Geshem sent to me, saying, "Come, let us meet together in the villages in the plain of Ono." But they were planning to do me harm.
verses.6:3: So I sent messengers to them, saying, "I am carrying out a great work, and I am not able to come down. Why should the work cease while I leave it and come down to you?"
verses.6:4: And they sent to me four times in this manner, and I answered them in the same manner.
verses.6:5: Then Sanballat sent his servant to me in this same manner a fifth time, with an open letter in his hand.
verses.6:6: In it was written, "It is reported among the nations, and Gashmu also says, that you and the Jews intend to rebel; therefore you are building the wall, and according to these reports you are to become their king.
verses.6:7: You have also appointed prophets to proclaim concerning you in Jerusalem, saying, 'There is a king in Judah!' Now it will be reported to the king according to these words. Come now, therefore, and let us take counsel together."
verses.6:8: Then I sent to him, saying, "No such things as you speak of have taken place, for you are inventing them out of your own heart."
verses.6:9: For all of them were trying to frighten us, saying, "Their hands will drop from the work, and it will not be done." Now therefore, strengthen my hands.
verses.6:10: Afterward I went to the house of Shemaiah the son of Delaiah, the son of Mehetabel, who was shut in; and he said, "Let us meet together in the house of God, within the temple, and let us shut the doors of the temple, for they are coming to slay you; indeed, at night they are coming to slay you."
verses.6:11: And I said, "Should a man such as I flee? And who is there such as I who would go into the temple and live? I will not go in."
verses.6:12: Then I discerned, and behold, God had not sent him; for he spoke this prophecy against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.
verses.6:13: For this purpose he was hired, that I might be afraid and act accordingly and sin, and so give them occasion for an evil report, that they might reproach me.
verses.6:14: Remember Tobiah and Sanballat, O my God, according to these works of theirs, and also Noadiah the prophetess and the rest of the prophets who were trying to frighten me.
verses.6:15: So the wall was finished on the twenty-fifth day of Elul, in fifty-two days.
verses.6:16: And it came to pass, when all our enemies heard of it and all the nations around us saw it, that they fell greatly in their own eyes; for they perceived that this work had been accomplished by our God.
verses.6:17: Moreover, in those days the nobles of Judah sent many letters to Tobiah, and letters from Tobiah came to them.
verses.6:18: For many in Judah were bound by oath to him, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah the son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam the son of Berechiah.
verses.6:19: They also kept speaking of his good deeds before me, and reported my words to him. And Tobiah sent letters to frighten me.
verses.7:1: Now it came to pass, after the wall had been built and I had set up the doors, that the gatekeepers, the singers, and the Levites were appointed.
verses.7:2: Then I gave my brother Hanani and Hananiah, the commander of the citadel, charge over Jerusalem; for he was a faithful man and feared God more than many.
verses.7:3: And I said to them, "The gates of Jerusalem shall not be opened until the sun grows hot; and while they are still standing guard, let them shut the doors and bar them; and appoint watches of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, each man at his watch and each man opposite his own house."
verses.7:4: Now the city was wide and great, yet the people within it were few, and no houses had been built.
verses.7:5: Then my God put it into my heart to gather the nobles, the officials, and the people to be enrolled by genealogy. And I found the book of the genealogy of those who had come up at the first, and found written in it:
verses.7:6: These are the people of the province who came up from the captivity of the exile, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away, and who returned to Jerusalem and to Judah, every man to his own city.
verses.7:7: They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:
verses.7:8: The sons of Parosh, two thousand one hundred and seventy-two.
verses.7:9: The sons of Shephatiah, three hundred and seventy-two.
verses.7:10: The sons of Arah, six hundred and fifty-two.
verses.7:11: The sons of Pahath-Moab, of the sons of Jeshua and Joab, two thousand eight hundred and eighteen.
verses.7:12: The sons of Elam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four.
verses.7:13: The sons of Zattu, eight hundred and forty-five.
verses.7:14: The sons of Zaccai, seven hundred and sixty.
verses.7:15: The sons of Binnui, six hundred and forty-eight.
verses.7:16: The sons of Bebai, six hundred and twenty-eight.
verses.7:17: The sons of Azgad, two thousand three hundred and twenty-two.
verses.7:18: The sons of Adonikam, six hundred and sixty-seven.
verses.7:19: The sons of Bigvai, two thousand and sixty-seven.
verses.7:20: The sons of Adin, six hundred and fifty-five.
verses.7:21: The sons of Ater, of Hezekiah, ninety-eight.
verses.7:22: The sons of Hashum, three hundred and twenty-eight.
verses.7:23: The sons of Bezai, three hundred and twenty-four.
verses.7:24: The sons of Hariph, one hundred and twelve.
verses.7:26: The men of Bethlehem and Netophah, one hundred and eighty-eight.
verses.7:27: The men of Anathoth, one hundred and twenty-eight.
verses.7:29: The men of Kiriath-Jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, seven hundred and forty-three.
verses.7:30: The men of Ramah and Geba, six hundred and twenty-one.
verses.7:31: The men of Michmas, one hundred and twenty-two.
verses.7:32: The men of Bethel and Ai, one hundred and twenty-three.
verses.7:33: The men of the other Nebo, fifty-two.
verses.7:34: The sons of the other Elam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four.
verses.7:35: The sons of Harim, three hundred and twenty.
verses.7:36: The sons of Jericho, three hundred and forty-five.
verses.7:37: The sons of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, seven hundred and twenty-one.
verses.7:38: The sons of Senaah, three thousand nine hundred and thirty.
verses.7:39: The priests: the sons of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred and seventy-three.
verses.7:40: The sons of Immer, one thousand and fifty-two.
verses.7:41: The sons of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred and forty-seven.
verses.7:42: The sons of Harim, one thousand and seventeen.
verses.7:43: The Levites: the sons of Jeshua, of Kadmiel, of the sons of Hodevah, seventy-four.
verses.7:44: The singers: the sons of Asaph, one hundred and forty-eight.
verses.7:45: The gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Ater, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Akkub, the sons of Hatita, and the sons of Shobai, one hundred and thirty-eight.
verses.7:46: The temple servants: the sons of Ziha, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabbaoth;
verses.7:47: the sons of Keros, the sons of Sia, the sons of Padon;
verses.7:48: the sons of Lebana, the sons of Hagaba, the sons of Shalmai;
verses.7:49: the sons of Hanan, the sons of Giddel, the sons of Gahar;
verses.7:50: the sons of Reaiah, the sons of Rezin, the sons of Nekoda;
verses.7:51: the sons of Gazzam, the sons of Uzza, the sons of Paseah;
verses.7:52: the sons of Besai, the sons of Meunim, the sons of Nephishesim;
verses.7:53: the sons of Bakbuk, the sons of Hakupha, the sons of Harhur;
verses.7:54: the sons of Bazlith, the sons of Mehida, the sons of Harsha;
verses.7:55: the sons of Barkos, the sons of Sisera, the sons of Temah;
verses.7:56: the sons of Neziah, and the sons of Hatipha.
verses.7:57: The sons of Solomon's servants: the sons of Sotai, the sons of Sophereth, the sons of Perida;
verses.7:58: the sons of Jaala, the sons of Darkon, the sons of Giddel;
verses.7:59: the sons of Shephatiah, the sons of Hattil, the sons of Pochereth-Hazzebaim, and the sons of Amon.
verses.7:60: All the temple servants and the sons of Solomon's servants were three hundred and ninety-two.
verses.7:61: And these were those who came up from Tel-Melah, Tel-Harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer; yet they could not prove their fathers' house or their descent, whether they were of Israel:
verses.7:62: the sons of Delaiah, the sons of Tobiah, and the sons of Nekoda, six hundred and forty-two.
verses.7:63: And of the priests: the sons of Hobaiah, the sons of Hakkoz, and the sons of Barzillai, who had taken a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.
verses.7:64: These searched for their record among those enrolled by genealogy, but it was not found; therefore they were excluded from the priesthood as defiled.
verses.7:65: And the governor said to them that they should not eat of the most holy things until a priest should arise with Urim and Thummim.
verses.7:66: The whole assembly together was forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty,
verses.7:67: besides their male and female servants, of whom there were seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven; and they had two hundred and forty-five male and female singers.
verses.7:69: Camels, four hundred and thirty-five; donkeys, six thousand seven hundred and twenty.
verses.7:70: Now some of the heads of the fathers' houses contributed to the work. The governor gave to the treasury one thousand gold darics, fifty basins, and five hundred and thirty priestly garments.
verses.7:71: And some of the heads of the fathers' houses gave to the treasury of the work twenty thousand gold darics and two thousand two hundred minas of silver.
verses.7:72: And what the rest of the people gave was twenty thousand gold darics, two thousand minas of silver, and sixty-seven priestly garments.
verses.7:73: So the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the temple servants, and all Israel dwelt in their cities. And when the seventh month came, the children of Israel were in their cities.
verses.8:1: Now all the people assembled as one man in the open square before the Water Gate; and they told Ezra the scribe to bring the Book of the Law of Moses, which the LORD had commanded Israel.
verses.8:2: So Ezra the priest brought the Law before the assembly of men and women, and all who could hear with understanding, on the first day of the seventh month.
verses.8:3: And he read from it facing the open square before the Water Gate, from daybreak until midday, in the presence of the men and the women and those who had understanding; and the ears of all the people were attentive to the Book of the Law.
verses.8:4: So Ezra the scribe stood upon a wooden platform that they had built for the occasion; and beside him stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah on his right hand, and on his left hand Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
verses.8:5: And Ezra opened the book in the sight of all the people, for he was elevated above all the people; and as he opened it, all the people stood up.
verses.8:6: Then Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God; and all the people answered, "Amen, Amen!" while lifting up their hands. Then they bowed low and worshiped the LORD with their faces to the ground.
verses.8:7: Also Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites helped the people understand the Law, while the people remained in their places.
verses.8:8: So they read distinctly from the book, in the Law of God, and gave the meaning, so that they understood what was read.
verses.8:9: And Nehemiah, who was the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who taught the people said to all the people, "This day is holy to the LORD your God; do not mourn or weep." For all the people were weeping when they heard the words of the Law.
verses.8:10: Then he said to them, "Go your way, eat rich delicacies and drink sweet beverages, and send portions to anyone for whom nothing is prepared; for this day is holy to our Lord. Do not grieve, for the joy of the LORD is your stronghold."
verses.8:11: So the Levites quieted all the people, saying, "Be still, for the day is holy; do not grieve."
verses.8:12: And all the people departed to eat and drink, to send portions, and to make great rejoicing, because they had understood the words that were declared to them.
verses.8:13: Now on the second day the heads of the fathers' houses of all the people, along with the priests and the Levites, assembled before Ezra the scribe to study the words of the Law.
verses.8:14: And they found written in the Law, which the LORD had commanded by the hand of Moses, that the children of Israel should dwell in booths during the feast of the seventh month,
verses.8:15: and that they should announce and send a proclamation through all their cities and in Jerusalem, saying, "Go out to the hill country and bring olive branches, wild olive branches, myrtle branches, palm branches, and branches of thick-leaved trees, to build booths, as it is written."
verses.8:16: So the people went out, brought them back, and constructed booths for themselves, each man upon his roof, in their courtyards, in the courts of the house of God, in the open square of the Water Gate, and in the open square of the Gate of Ephraim.
verses.8:17: Thus the whole assembly of those who had returned from the captivity made booths and dwelt in the booths; for since the days of Joshua the son of Nun until that day, the children of Israel had not done so. And there was exceedingly great gladness.
verses.8:18: Day by day, from the first day until the last day, he read from the Book of the Law of God. And they kept the feast for seven days; and on the eighth day there was a solemn assembly, according to the ordinance.
verses.9:1: Now on the twenty-fourth day of this month, the children of Israel assembled with fasting, clad in sackcloth, and with earth upon them.
verses.9:2: Then the seed of Israel separated themselves from all foreigners; and they stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.
verses.9:3: And they stood up in their places and read from the Book of the Law of the LORD their God for one-fourth of the day; and for another fourth they made confession and worshiped the LORD their God.
verses.9:4: Then Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani stood upon the stairs of the Levites and cried out with a loud voice to the LORD their God.
verses.9:5: And the Levites—Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah—said, "Arise and bless the LORD your God from everlasting to everlasting! And let them bless Your glorious name, which is exalted above all blessing and praise!
verses.9:6: You alone are the LORD; You have made the heavens, the heaven of heavens with all their host, the earth and everything upon it, the seas and all that is in them. You preserve them all in life, and the host of heaven worships You.
verses.9:7: You are the LORD God, who chose Abram, brought him forth from Ur of the Chaldeans, and gave him the name Abraham.
verses.9:8: You found his heart faithful before You, and You made a covenant with him to give the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, and the Girgashites—to give it to his seed. And You have established Your words, for You are righteous.
verses.9:9: You saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt, and You heard their cry by the Red Sea.
verses.9:10: You performed signs and wonders against Pharaoh, against all his servants, and against all the people of his land, for You knew that they dealt arrogantly with them; and You made a name for Yourself, as it is to this day.
verses.9:11: You divided the sea before them, so that they passed through the midst of the sea on dry ground; and their pursuers You cast into the depths, like a stone into mighty waters.
verses.9:12: By a pillar of cloud You led them by day, and by a pillar of fire by night, to light for them the way in which they should walk.
verses.9:13: You descended also upon Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven; and You gave them upright ordinances and laws of truth, good statutes and commandments.
verses.9:14: You made known to them Your holy Sabbath, and commanded them precepts, statutes, and law by the hand of Your servant Moses.
verses.9:15: You gave them bread from heaven for their hunger, and brought forth water for them out of the rock for their thirst; and You told them to enter in to possess the land which You had lifted up Your hand to give them.
verses.9:16: Yet they and our fathers acted arrogantly; they stiffened their necks and did not hearken to Your commandments.
verses.9:17: They refused to obey and did not remember Your wondrous works that You had performed among them; instead they stiffened their necks, and in their rebellion appointed a leader to return to their bondage. Yet You are a God of forgiveness, gracious and merciful, slow to anger and abundant in lovingkindness, and You did not forsake them.
verses.9:18: Even when they made a molten calf for themselves and said, 'This is your god who brought you up out of Egypt,' and committed great blasphemies,
verses.9:19: yet You, in Your abundant mercies, did not forsake them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud did not depart from over them by day to guide them along the way, nor the pillar of fire by night to give them light and show them the path in which they should walk.
verses.9:20: You also gave Your good Spirit to instruct them, and You did not withhold Your manna from their mouths, and You gave them water for their thirst.
verses.9:21: For forty years You sustained them in the wilderness, so that they lacked nothing; their garments did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.
verses.9:22: You also gave them kingdoms and peoples and allotted them into every district; so they took possession of the land of Sihon, even the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan.
verses.9:23: You multiplied their children like the stars of heaven, and brought them into the land concerning which You had told their fathers to enter and possess it.
verses.9:24: So the children went in and possessed the land; and You subdued before them the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and delivered them into their hand, along with their kings and the peoples of the land, to do with them according to their pleasure.
verses.9:25: They captured fortified cities and fertile soil, and took possession of houses filled with every good thing, hewn cisterns, vineyards, olive groves, and fruit trees in abundance. So they ate, were filled, grew fat, and reveled in Your great goodness.
verses.9:26: Nevertheless they were defiant and rebelled against You; they cast Your Law behind their backs, slew Your prophets who warned them to turn back to You, and committed great blasphemies.
verses.9:27: Therefore You gave them into the hand of their adversaries, who afflicted them; yet in the time of their distress they cried out to You, and You heard from heaven, and according to Your abundant mercies You gave them deliverers who saved them out of the hand of their adversaries.
verses.9:28: Yet as soon as they had rest, they returned to doing evil before You. Therefore You abandoned them into the hand of their enemies, so that they ruled over them; yet when they turned and cried out to You, You heard from heaven, and many times You rescued them according to Your mercies.
verses.9:29: And You warned them in order to bring them back to Your Law. Yet they acted presumptuously and did not obey Your commandments, but sinned against Your ordinances—by which a man shall live if he does them—and they turned a stubborn shoulder, stiffened their necks, and would not listen.
verses.9:30: Yet for many years You were patient with them and admonished them by Your Spirit through Your prophets, but they would not give ear. Therefore You delivered them into the hand of the peoples of the lands.
verses.9:31: Nevertheless, in Your abundant mercies You did not make a full end of them nor forsake them; for You are a gracious and merciful God.
verses.9:32: Now therefore, our God—the great, the mighty, and the awesome God, who keeps covenant and lovingkindness—do not let all the hardship seem small before You that has come upon us, upon our kings, our princes, our priests, our prophets, our fathers, and all Your people, from the days of the kings of Assyria to this day.
verses.9:33: Yet You are righteous in all that has befallen us; for You have dealt in truth, while we have acted wickedly.
verses.9:34: Neither our kings, our princes, our priests, nor our fathers have kept Your Law, nor have they paid heed to Your commandments and Your testimonies with which You warned them.
verses.9:35: Even in their own kingdom, amid the great goodness that You bestowed upon them, and in the spacious and fertile land that You set before them, they did not serve You, nor did they turn from their evil deeds.
verses.9:36: Behold, we are servants this day; and as for the land that You gave to our fathers to eat its fruit and its bounty, behold, we are servants upon it.
verses.9:37: Its rich yield increases for the kings whom You have set over us because of our sins; they also rule over our bodies and over our livestock at their pleasure, and we are in great distress."
verses.10:1: And because of all this, we make a sure covenant and set it in writing; and upon the sealed document are our leaders, our Levites, and our priests.
verses.10:2: Now those who placed their seal on the document were Nehemiah the governor, the son of Hachaliah, and Zedekiah;
verses.10:9: Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah—these were the priests.
verses.10:10: And the Levites: Jeshua the son of Azaniah, Binnui of the sons of Henadad, and Kadmiel;
verses.10:11: and their brethren: Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,
verses.10:15: The chiefs of the people: Parosh, Pahath-Moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani,
verses.10:29: Now the rest of the people—the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the temple servants, and all who had separated themselves from the peoples of the lands to the Law of God, with their wives, their sons, and their daughters, everyone who had knowledge and understanding—
verses.10:30: joined firmly with their brethren, their nobles, and entered into a curse and an oath to walk in the Law of God, which was given by the hand of Moses the servant of God, and to keep and perform all the commandments of the LORD our Lord, and His judgments and His statutes:
verses.10:31: that we will not give our daughters to the peoples of the land, nor take their daughters for our sons;
verses.10:32: and if the peoples of the land bring wares or any grain on the Sabbath day to sell, we will not buy from them on the Sabbath or on a holy day; and we will forego the seventh year and the exaction of every debt.
verses.10:33: Also we have established ordinances upon ourselves to contribute one-third of a shekel yearly for the service of the house of our God:
verses.10:34: for the showbread, for the continual grain offering, for the continual burnt offering, for the Sabbaths, the New Moons, and the appointed feasts, for the holy things, and for the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God.
verses.10:35: We have also cast lots—the priests, the Levites, and the people—for the wood offering, to bring it to the house of our God, according to our fathers' houses, at appointed times year by year, to burn upon the altar of the LORD our God, as it is written in the Law.
verses.10:36: We also obligate ourselves to bring the firstfruits of our ground and the firstfruits of all fruit of every tree, year by year, to the house of the LORD;
verses.10:37: also to bring the firstborn of our sons and of our livestock, as it is written in the Law, and the firstborn of our herds and our flocks, to the house of our God, to the priests who minister in the house of our God;
verses.10:38: and we will bring the first of our dough, our contributions, the fruit of every tree, the new wine, and the oil to the priests, to the chambers of the house of our God, and the tithe of our ground to the Levites; for the Levites themselves are the ones who collect the tithes in all the cities of our labor.
verses.10:39: And the priest, the son of Aaron, shall be with the Levites when the Levites receive the tithes; and the Levites shall bring up the tithe of the tithe to the house of our God, to the chambers of the storehouse.
verses.10:40: For the children of Israel and the sons of Levi shall bring the contribution of the grain, the new wine, and the oil to the chambers, where the vessels of the sanctuary are, together with the priests who minister, the gatekeepers, and the singers; thus we will not neglect the house of our God.
verses.11:1: Now the leaders of the people dwelt in Jerusalem; and the rest of the people cast lots to bring one out of ten to dwell in Jerusalem, the holy city, while the other nine parts remained in the cities.
verses.11:2: And the people blessed all the men who willingly offered themselves to dwell in Jerusalem.
verses.11:3: Now these are the chiefs of the province who dwelt in Jerusalem; but in the cities of Judah everyone dwelt in his own possession in their cities—Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple servants, and the sons of Solomon's servants.
verses.11:4: And in Jerusalem dwelt some of the sons of Judah and some of the sons of Benjamin. Of the sons of Judah: Athaiah the son of Uzziah, the son of Zechariah, the son of Amariah, the son of Shephatiah, the son of Mahalalel, of the sons of Perez;
verses.11:5: and Maaseiah the son of Baruch, the son of Col-Hozeh, the son of Hazaiah, the son of Adaiah, the son of Joiarib, the son of Zechariah, the son of the Shilonite.
verses.11:6: All the sons of Perez who dwelt in Jerusalem were four hundred and sixty-eight valiant men.
verses.11:7: And these are the sons of Benjamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Joed, the son of Pedaiah, the son of Kolaiah, the son of Maaseiah, the son of Ithiel, the son of Jeshaiah;
verses.11:8: and after him Gabbai and Sallai, nine hundred and twenty-eight.
verses.11:9: And Joel the son of Zichri was overseer over them, and Judah the son of Hassenuah was second over the city.
verses.11:10: Of the priests: Jedaiah the son of Joiarib, and Jachin;
verses.11:11: Seraiah the son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the ruler of the house of God;
verses.11:12: and their brethren who did the work of the house, eight hundred and twenty-two; and Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pelaliah, the son of Amzi, the son of Zechariah, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchijah;
verses.11:13: and his brethren, heads of fathers' houses, two hundred and forty-two; and Amashsai the son of Azarel, the son of Ahzai, the son of Meshillemoth, the son of Immer;
verses.11:14: and their brethren, mighty men of valor, one hundred and twenty-eight; and their overseer was Zabdiel the son of Haggedolim.
verses.11:15: And of the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Bunni;
verses.11:17: and Mattaniah the son of Mica, the son of Zabdi, the son of Asaph, the leader who began the thanksgiving in prayer, and Bakbukiah, the second among his brethren, and Abda the son of Shammua, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun.
verses.11:18: All the Levites in the holy city were two hundred and eighty-four.
verses.11:19: And the gatekeepers: Akkub, Talmon, and their brethren who kept watch at the gates were one hundred and seventy-two.
verses.11:22: And the overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi the son of Bani, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Mica, of the sons of Asaph, the singers, over the work of the house of God.
verses.11:23: For there was a command from the king concerning them, and a fixed provision for the singers, as each day required.
verses.11:24: And Pethahiah the son of Meshezabel, of the sons of Zerah the son of Judah, was at the king's hand in all matters concerning the people.
verses.11:25: And as for the villages with their fields, some of the sons of Judah dwelt in Kiriath-Arba and its surrounding towns, in Dibon and its surrounding towns, in Jekabzeel and its villages,
verses.11:26: in Jeshua, in Moladah, in Beth-Pelet,
verses.11:27: in Hazar-Shual, and in Beersheba and its surrounding towns.
verses.11:30: Zanoah, Adullam, and their villages, Lachish and its fields, and Azekah and its surrounding towns. Thus they encamped from Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom.
verses.11:31: And the sons of Benjamin dwelt from Geba onward, at Michmash, Aija, and Bethel and its surrounding towns.
verses.11:36: And certain divisions of the Levites in Judah were assigned to Benjamin.
verses.12:1: Now these are the priests and the Levites who came up with Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
verses.12:7: Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and Jedaiah. These were the heads of the priests and their brethren in the days of Jeshua.
verses.12:8: Moreover, the Levites were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah, who was over the songs of thanksgiving, he and his brethren.
verses.12:9: Also Bakbukiah and Unni, their brethren, stood opposite them in their watches.
verses.12:10: Jeshua fathered Joiakim, and Joiakim fathered Eliashib, and Eliashib fathered Joiada;
verses.12:11: and Joiada fathered Jonathan, and Jonathan fathered Jaddua.
verses.12:12: Now in the days of Joiakim, the priests, the heads of the fathers' houses, were: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah;
verses.12:13: of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan;
verses.12:14: of Melicu, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph;
verses.12:15: of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai;
verses.12:16: of Iddo, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam;
verses.12:17: of Abijah, Zichri; of Miniamin; of Moadiah, Piltai;
verses.12:18: of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jehonathan;
verses.12:19: and of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi;
verses.12:20: of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber;
verses.12:21: of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah, Nethanel.
verses.12:22: The Levites in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua were recorded as heads of fathers' houses, and also the priests, during the reign of Darius the Persian.
verses.12:23: The sons of Levi, the heads of the fathers' houses, were written in the book of the chronicles, even until the days of Johanan the son of Eliashib.
verses.12:24: And the heads of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua the son of Kadmiel, with their brethren opposite them, to praise and to give thanks, according to the commandment of David the man of God, watch opposite watch.
verses.12:25: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers keeping the watch at the storehouses of the gates.
verses.12:26: These were in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor, and of Ezra the priest, the scribe.
verses.12:27: Now at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, they sought out the Levites from all their places to bring them to Jerusalem to celebrate the dedication with gladness, both with thanksgivings and with singing, with cymbals, harps, and lyres.
verses.12:28: And the sons of the singers gathered together from the surrounding region around Jerusalem, and from the villages of the Netophathites,
verses.12:29: and from Beth-gilgal, and from the fields of Geba and Azmaveth; for the singers had built villages for themselves all around Jerusalem.
verses.12:30: Then the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people, and the gates, and the wall.
verses.12:31: Then I brought the princes of Judah up upon the wall, and I appointed two great thanksgiving choirs to go in procession. One went to the right upon the wall toward the Dung Gate;
verses.12:32: and after them went Hoshaiah and half of the princes of Judah,
verses.12:35: and some of the sons of the priests with trumpets: Zechariah the son of Jonathan, the son of Shemaiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Micaiah, the son of Zaccur, the son of Asaph,
verses.12:36: and his brethren, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani, with the musical instruments of David the man of God; and Ezra the scribe went before them.
verses.12:37: At the Fountain Gate, straight ahead of them, they went up by the stairs of the City of David, at the ascent of the wall, above the house of David, as far as the Water Gate on the east.
verses.12:38: And the second thanksgiving choir went in the opposite direction, and I followed after it with half of the people upon the wall, above the Tower of the Ovens, as far as the Broad Wall,
verses.12:39: and above the Gate of Ephraim, and by the Old Gate, and by the Fish Gate, and the Tower of Hananel, and the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Sheep Gate; and they halted at the Gate of the Guard.
verses.12:40: So the two thanksgiving choirs took their stand in the house of God, and I and half of the rulers with me,
verses.12:41: and the priests, Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, with trumpets,
verses.12:42: also Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. And the singers sang aloud, with Jezrahiah as their overseer.
verses.12:43: And on that day they offered great sacrifices and rejoiced, for God had made them rejoice with exceeding joy; the women and the children also rejoiced, and the rejoicing of Jerusalem was heard from afar.
verses.12:44: On that day men were appointed over the chambers for the storehouses, the contributions, the firstfruits, and the tithes, to gather into them from the fields of the cities the portions prescribed by the Law for the priests and for the Levites; for Judah rejoiced over the priests and over the Levites who ministered.
verses.12:45: And they kept the charge of their God and the charge of purification, as did the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the commandment of David and of Solomon his son.
verses.12:46: For in the days of David and Asaph of old, there were leaders of the singers, and songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.
verses.12:47: And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah gave the portions for the singers and the gatekeepers as each day required; and they set apart the consecrated portions for the Levites, and the Levites set apart the consecrated portions for the sons of Aaron.
verses.13:1: On that day the Book of Moses was read in the hearing of the people, and it was found written in it that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God,
verses.13:2: for they failed to meet the children of Israel with bread and with water, and hired Balaam against them to invoke a curse on them; yet our God turned the curse into a blessing.
verses.13:3: Now it came to pass, when they heard the law, that they separated all the mixed multitude from Israel.
verses.13:4: Now before this, Eliashib the priest, who was appointed over the chamber of the house of our God, was closely related to Tobiah.
verses.13:5: And he prepared for him a great chamber, where previously they had stored the grain offerings, the frankincense, the vessels, and the tithes of grain, new wine, and oil, which were commanded for the Levites, the singers, and the gatekeepers, as well as the offerings for the priests.
verses.13:6: But during all this I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I had gone to the king. Then after some time I asked leave of the king.
verses.13:7: And I came to Jerusalem and perceived the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah, in preparing a chamber for him in the courts of the house of God.
verses.13:8: And it grieved me bitterly; therefore I cast all the household goods of Tobiah out of the chamber.
verses.13:9: Then I gave command, and they cleansed the chambers; and I brought back there the vessels of the house of God, with the grain offering and the frankincense.
verses.13:10: I also learned that the portions of the Levites had not been given to them; for the Levites and the singers who performed the service had fled, each to his own field.
verses.13:11: So I contended with the rulers and said, "Why is the house of God forsaken?" And I gathered them together and set them at their posts.
verses.13:12: Then all Judah brought the tithe of the grain, the new wine, and the oil into the storehouses.
verses.13:13: And I appointed as treasurers over the storehouses Shelemiah the priest and Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites; and at their side was Hanan the son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah; for they were esteemed faithful, and their duty was to distribute to their brethren.
verses.13:14: Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and do not blot out my faithful deeds that I have done for the house of my God and for its services.
verses.13:15: In those days I saw men in Judah treading winepresses on the Sabbath, bringing in heaps of grain, and loading donkeys with them, as well as wine, grapes, figs, and all manner of burdens, which they brought into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. And I warned them on the day they sold provisions.
verses.13:16: Men of Tyre also dwelt in it, who brought in fish and all kinds of merchandise, and sold them on the Sabbath to the children of Judah, and in Jerusalem.
verses.13:17: Then I contended with the nobles of Judah and said to them, "What is this evil thing that you are doing, profaning the Sabbath day?
verses.13:18: Did not your fathers do thus, and did not our God bring all this calamity upon us and upon this city? Yet you bring added wrath upon Israel by profaning the Sabbath!"
verses.13:19: And it came to pass, as the shadows fell upon the gates of Jerusalem before the Sabbath, that I commanded the doors to be shut, and gave orders that they should not be opened until after the Sabbath. And I stationed some of my servants at the gates, so that no burden would enter on the Sabbath day.
verses.13:20: Now the merchants and sellers of all kinds of wares lodged outside Jerusalem once or twice.
verses.13:21: Then I warned them and said to them, "Why do you lodge in front of the wall? If you do so again, I will lay hands on you!" From that time on they came no more on the Sabbath.
verses.13:22: And I commanded the Levites that they should purify themselves, and come and guard the gates, to sanctify the Sabbath day. Remember me, O my God, concerning this also, and spare me according to the abundance of Your lovingkindness.
verses.13:23: In those days I also saw Jews who had married Ashdodite, Ammonite, and Moabite women.
verses.13:24: And half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod, and could not speak the language of Judah, but spoke according to the language of each respective people.
verses.13:25: So I contended with them and cursed them, struck some of the men and pulled out their hair, and made them swear by God, saying, "You shall not give your daughters to their sons, nor take of their daughters for your sons or for yourselves.
verses.13:26: Did not Solomon king of Israel sin by these things? Yet among many nations there was no king like him, who was beloved by his God; and God made him king over all Israel. Nevertheless, foreign women caused even him to sin.
verses.13:27: Should we then listen to you and do all this great evil, acting unfaithfully against our God by marrying foreign women?"
verses.13:28: And one of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was a son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite; therefore I drove him away from me.
verses.13:29: Remember them, O my God, because they have defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites.
verses.13:30: Thus I cleansed them of everything foreign, and I appointed duties for the priests and the Levites, each in his service,
verses.13:31: and for the wood offering at appointed times, and for the firstfruits. Remember me, O my God, for good!

notes.1:1: Chislev was the ninth month of the Hebrew calendar, corresponding to November and December; the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes I fell in 445 BC.
notes.1:9: The Hebrew text has a minor ketiv/qere spelling variant for the verb meaning "and I will bring them," with the qere reading followed here.
notes.1:11: A royal cupbearer was not merely an attendant but a high-ranking, trusted court official with direct daily access to the king.
notes.2:1: Nisan was the first month of the Hebrew calendar, corresponding to March and April, about four months after the events of chapter one.
notes.2:8: Hebrew pardes ("forest") is a Persian loanword referring to a royal timber preserve or enclosed park.
notes.2:10: The title "official" renders Hebrew ha-eved, literally "the servant," a standard designation for an appointed royal administrator.
notes.2:13: The Hebrew displays a ketiv/qere word-division variant for "which were broken down," with the qere reading followed here; "Dragon Well" literally renders En ha-Tannin, sometimes understood as "Jackal Well."
notes.3:5: Hebrew adonaihem ("their lords") can refer either to the human supervisors directing the work or, as a plural of majesty, to God ("their Lord").
notes.3:15: The ketiv reads plural "and they set up," while the qere followed here reads singular "and set up" to agree with Shallun; the Pool of Shelah is the Pool of Siloam.
notes.3:20: The ketiv spells the father's name "Zabbai," whereas the qere followed here reads "Zaccai."
notes.3:26: "Temple servants" translates Hebrew Nethinim, literally "the given ones," a guild of dedicated assistants to the Levites who resided on Ophel.
notes.3:30: Here and in verse thirty-one, the ketiv reads "after me," while the qere followed in the translation reads "after him."
notes.3:33: In Masoretic Hebrew versification, verses thirty-three through thirty-seven belong to chapter three rather than opening chapter four.
notes.4:1: In the Masoretic Hebrew versification followed here, Nehemiah 4:1–17 corresponds to 4:7–23 in most English Bibles. The Hebrew idiom translated "the restoration ... was advancing" literally reads "healing went up."
notes.4:6: The Hebrew clause is notably terse and elliptical, literally reading "from all the places where you return, against us," conveying that enemies threatened from every direction.
notes.4:7: Translates the Qere ("in the exposed places"); the Ketiv displays a slightly different spelling of the same rare noun.
notes.4:9: Translates the Qere (wayyiqtol "we returned"); the Ketiv writes the full vowel spelling with waw.
notes.4:17: The final Hebrew phrase is extremely compressed, literally "each man his weapon the water," indicating that the men kept their weapons with them even when going for water.
notes.5:7: Translates the Qere ("exacting interest," from the root nashah); the Ketiv spells the participle with aleph, reflecting a common orthographic variation between nashah and nasa.
notes.5:9: Translates the Qere ("And I said," first-person singular); the Ketiv reads third-person singular ("and he said").
notes.5:11: "The hundredth part" refers to a one-percent rate of interest, likely charged monthly on loans of silver and agricultural produce.
notes.5:14: "The bread of the governor" refers to the customary food allowance and tax revenue allotted to maintain the Persian provincial governor and his household.
notes.6:2: The Hebrew term translated "in the villages" (bakkefirim) may alternatively represent a specific town name, Chephirim, in the plain of Ono.
notes.6:6: "Gashmu" preserves the Hebrew letter's variant spelling of the name Geshem (compare verse 1), reflecting an Arabic nominative ending.
notes.6:9: "Now therefore, strengthen my hands" is a brief petition directed to God, whose name is implied rather than explicitly stated in the Hebrew text.
notes.7:3: The Masoretic Qere reads "And I said" (first person, continuing Nehemiah's memoir), whereas the Ketiv reads "and he said."
notes.7:4: Literally "broad of hands," a Hebrew idiom denoting spaciousness and wide extent.
notes.7:6: This genealogical register parallels the list in Ezra 2, with several minor differences in clan totals and name spellings that are preserved faithfully from the Hebrew text of Nehemiah.
notes.7:46: Hebrew "Nethinim," literally "those given," referring to hereditary attendants appointed to temple service.
notes.7:52: The Masoretic Qere reads "Nephishesim," whereas the Ketiv reads "Nephushesim."
notes.7:65: Hebrew "Tirshatha," a Persian official title for the provincial governor.
notes.7:69: The Masoretic text followed here passes directly from verse 67 to verse 69, without the tally of horses and mules present in Ezra 2:66 and in some manuscripts.
notes.8:8: Hebrew mephorash can mean "distinctly" or "with interpretation," indicating that the Levites read the Law clearly and explained its meaning to the assembly.
notes.8:9: The Hebrew title hat-tirshatha ("the Tirshatha") is a Persian loanword designating the provincial governor.
notes.8:10: Hebrew ma'uzzekem means "your stronghold" or "your place of refuge," often rendered "your strength."
notes.8:17: The Hebrew text uses the post-exilic spelling Jeshua for Joshua the son of Nun.
notes.9:6: Following the Qere attah ("You"); the Ketiv writes the shorter defective form at.
notes.9:9: Hebrew yam-suph literally means "Sea of Reeds," traditionally rendered "Red Sea."
notes.9:17: Following the Qere we-rab-hesed ("and abundant in lovingkindness"); the Ketiv reads we-hesed ("and lovingkindness"). The Hebrew text also reads "in their rebellion" rather than "in Egypt."
notes.9:22: Hebrew le-pe'ah literally means "to a corner" or "by border," indicating the allotment of territories into districts or to their farthest bounds.
notes.10:1: Masoretic versification places this verse at the beginning of chapter 10, corresponding to 9:38 in many English Bibles and shifting the remaining verse numbers of chapter 10 by one.
notes.10:2: The Hebrew title hattirshatha is a Persian loanword designating the provincial governor.
notes.10:20: The qere reads Nebai, followed in the translation; the ketiv reads Nobai.
notes.10:29: Hebrew Nethinim denotes dedicated temple servants who assisted the Levites in sanctuary duties.
notes.11:14: The expression "the son of Haggedolim" literally means "the son of the great ones" and may denote a prominent family or rank.
notes.11:17: The qere reads Jeduthun, followed in the translation; the ketiv reads Jedithun.
notes.11:25: Hebrew literally reads "its daughters," an idiom referring to smaller dependent towns surrounding a chief city.
notes.12:9: The Qere reads Unni; the Ketiv reads Unno.
notes.12:14: The Qere reads Melicu; the Ketiv reads Malluchi.
notes.12:16: The Qere reads Iddo; the Ketiv reads Adaiah.
notes.12:17: The Masoretic Hebrew text leaves the name of the head of the house of Miniamin unstated before the entry for Moadiah.
notes.12:46: The Qere reads the plural leaders; the Ketiv reads the singular leader.
notes.13:6: Artaxerxes I is called king of Babylon as ruler of the Persian Empire, which encompassed Babylon; his thirty-second year corresponds to 433 BC.
notes.13:19: The verb translated as the shadows fell refers to the deepening dusk at the gates of Jerusalem just before the Sabbath began at sundown.
notes.13:23: The Masoretic text notes an orthographic ketiv/qere variation in the spellings of Ashdodite and Ammonite, with the qere using the shorter vocalized forms without changing the meaning.
notes.13:25: Hebrew oath clauses introduced by if express an emphatic prohibition, rendered here as you shall not.
